contentHtml:
KENYA—Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale has opened the 9th Kenya International Cancer Conference in Mombasa County, bringing together healthcare professionals, policymakers, and development partners to discuss ways to improve access to cancer prevention, diagnosis and treatment.

Organised by the Kenya Society of Haematology and Oncology (KESHO), the three-day conference is being held under the theme “Equity, Excellence and Sustainable Impact in Cancer Care.”

Discussions focus on strengthening cancer services through improved financing, early detection, specialist training, research and healthcare infrastructure.

Government increases cancer treatment funding

Kenya records 35,867 new cancer cases and 22,888 related deaths annually.

In response, the government is expanding access to affordable and specialised cancer services under its Universal Health Coverage (UHC) agenda.

According to Duale, 33.7 million Kenyans have registered with the Social Health Authority (SHA), with 53,465 patients accessing cancer treatment through the scheme.

To reduce out-of-pocket expenditure, the government increased the oncology benefit limit from KSh 550,000 (US$4,231) to KSh 800,000 (US$6,154) per patient, effective December 1, 2025.

It has also disbursed KSh 11.6 billion (US$89.2 million) to healthcare facilities to settle oncology claims.

The government is also expanding cancer treatment infrastructure. Six comprehensive cancer care centres have been established nationally, while at least 13 counties operate oncology programmes.

In addition, the Tobacco Control Fund is supporting the servicing and maintenance of radiotherapy machines to minimise disruptions to treatment.

Medicine affordability and digital financing reforms

Supply chain improvements at the Kenya Medical Supplies Authority (KEMSA) have raised order fill rates to more than 90% for most products.

Meanwhile, partnerships with pharmaceutical companies are reducing the cost of specialised cancer medicines.

An agreement with Pfizer has lowered the prices of nine innovative cancer medicines by between 70% and 90%.

Collaboration with Roche has also reduced the price of Herceptin for eligible breast cancer patients covered by SHA from KSh 120,000 (US $923) to KSh 40,000 (US$308) per session.

To strengthen accountability in cancer financing, the Government is digitising the implementation of the National Cancer Control Protocol through the Digital Health Agency (DHA) and the SHA Oncology Module.

The system provides for oncologist-led treatment authorisation, specialist-supervised care plans, single pre-authorization for approved treatment plans and continuous patient records.

These measures are intended to improve coordination between healthcare providers, streamline claims processing and strengthen oversight of public spending on cancer treatment.

Early detection and specialist workforce

At the community level, more than 107,000 Community Health Promoters (CHPs) are mobilising households to support early screening and detection.

More than four million girls have also received the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine, which helps prevent cervical cancer.

The Government is developing a funded National Cancer Screening Programme guided by the National Cancer Control Strategy and the Cervical Cancer Elimination Plan.

However, Kenya has fewer than 100 cancer specialists nationally, highlighting the need to expand specialist training, improve workforce distribution and strengthen staff retention.

Duale also emphasised investments in patient safety, cancer research and local manufacturing as priorities for improving access to cancer services.

The government is pursuing partnerships with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), the World Health Organization (WHO), and the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) to support cancer prevention, diagnosis, treatment, research and workforce development.

The conference was attended by the Ministry of Health Director of Family Health, Dr Bashir Issak; KESHO President Dr Gladwell Kiarie; SHA Board Chairperson Dr Abdi Mohammed; and National Cancer Institute of Kenya Chief Executive Officer Dr Elias Melly, among other stakeholders.
